chunks: Saad narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Sulayman, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He was asked about a man in the countryside who is unable to provide Fitrah, so he said: 'Let him give charity with four Artals of milk.'

key_terms.أَرْطَالٍ: Artals, a unit of volume/weight measurement
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the alms-tax given at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the alternative for Zakat al-Fitr if one cannot provide grain?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), illustrating the jurisprudential principle of *al-mutabadil* (exchangeability) where a non-grain staple can substitute for the standard Fitrah when access to wheat or barley is limited. This specific measurement of four *Artals* of milk highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh to accommodate the economic and geographical realities of rural dwellers (*ahl al-badiyah*), ensuring the obligation remains accessible without imposing undue hardship.
